stem: A family member asks a clinician to release separately maintained psychotherapy notes without the patient's authorization. Which HIPAA principle is most accurate?

options.A: Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed whenever another person requests health information because they receive the same disclosure treatment as routine medical records.
options.B: Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed freely for treatment purposes because HIPAA never requires authorization when information is requested by another clinician.
options.C: Psychotherapy notes receive special protection, and with limited exceptions HIPAA generally requires the patient's authorization before use or disclosure.
options.D: Psychotherapy notes fall outside HIPAA because they are kept separately from the medical record, so federal privacy requirements do not apply to their release.

rationale: 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2) requires a covered entity to obtain authorization for uses or disclosures of psychotherapy notes except for limited enumerated circumstances. HHS also explains that separately maintained psychotherapy notes receive special protection and, with few exceptions, patient authorization is required before disclosure, including treatment disclosure to a clinician other than the note originator. C therefore states the rule accurately. A treats psychotherapy notes like ordinary records, B incorrectly creates a blanket treatment exception, and D incorrectly treats separate maintenance as exclusion from HIPAA.
educational_objective: Recognize that HIPAA gives separately maintained psychotherapy notes special protection and generally requires patient authorization for use or disclosure, subject to limited regulatory exceptions.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office for Civil Rights; 45 CFR Part 164
source_document_title: HIPAA Privacy Rule — 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2); HHS FAQ: Does HIPAA provide extra protections for mental health information compared with other health information?

source_claim_supported: Psychotherapy notes are specially protected; a covered entity generally must obtain patient authorization for use or disclosure, subject to limited enumerated exceptions; treatment disclosure to another clinician generally still requires authorization.

source_original.stem: A family member asks a clinician to release separately maintained psychotherapy notes without the patient's authorization. Which HIPAA principle is most accurate?

options.A: Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed whenever another person requests health information, because they receive the same disclosure treatment as routine records.
options.B: Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed freely for treatment purposes, because HIPAA never requires authorization when information is requested by another clinician.
options.C: Psychotherapy notes receive special protection, and with limited exceptions HIPAA generally requires patient authorization before they are disclosed in most cases.
options.D: Psychotherapy notes fall outside HIPAA because they are kept separately from the medical record, so federal privacy requirements do not apply to their release at all.

source_original.rationale: HHS explains that psychotherapy notes are specially protected and generally require patient authorization before disclosure, subject to limited exceptions. Option C states that rule. Option A incorrectly treats psychotherapy notes like routine records. Option B incorrectly assumes treatment-purpose disclosure is automatically allowed to another clinician. Option D incorrectly claims that separate storage removes the notes from HIPAA protection.
source_original.source_detail: 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2) / HHS HIPAA guidance on psychotherapy notes: authorization is generally required for use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes, subject to limited enumerated exceptions; psychotherapy notes receive protections beyond ordinary medical records. correction_summary: Resolved prior BLOCKED status after live verification of 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2) and current HHS guidance. Tightened option C to 'use or disclosure' and removed redundant wording while preserving the limited-exceptions qualifier.

audit_findings.currentness: Current regulation and current HHS resources live in 2026; medical-record page reviewed 2025-05-30.
audit_findings.exact_locator: 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2); HHS FAQ 2088 and HIPAA Privacy Rule Summary, Psychotherapy Notes.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Authorization rule and limited exceptions verified directly; treatment disclosure to another provider is not generalized as freely permitted.

distractor_audit.A: Psychotherapy notes receive extra protection, not routine-record treatment.
distractor_audit.B: False blanket treatment exception; HHS says disclosure to provider other than originator generally requires authorization.
distractor_audit.D: Separate maintenance is part of the definition and does not put notes outside HIPAA.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C accurately preserves both the general authorization rule and limited exceptions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options test the same HIPAA distinction and no second legal interpretation is supportable.
audit_findings.blueprint: Confidentiality/privacy/client rights under Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: High-stakes legal second pass checked regulation text and HHS explanatory guidance separately; no unresolved conflict remains.
